overview.heading: Learning outcomes
overview.text:
In this programme, you learn how complex technology systems are designed, built, and operated using core principles from science and engineering. You gain experience in combining hardware, software, data, and human factors to develop reliable systems used in real‑world applications across diverse engineering domains.
Photo: Ellen Johanne Jarli / Jarli & Jordan.

objectives.heading: Knowledge
objectives.text:
After completing this programme, you will have
an understanding of complex technology-related challenges within the context of systems science and engineering:
You understand the complexity of real-world technology-related challenges.
You are familiar with the main principles of systems science and engineering.
You demonstrate in-depth understanding of systems thinking approaches.
You have specialised knowledge within one or more technology systems domains, such as renewable energy, robotics, space technology, societal security, and healthcare systems.
a solid foundation in the core technology domains, including
fundamental principles of programming, mathematics, physics, data science, and artificial intelligence, and how to apply them in different technology systems
ethical, legal, societal, economic, and environmental considerations related to various technology systems
innovation and sustainability in the context of technological development and change

objectives.heading: Skills
objectives.text:
After completing this programme, you will have
the ability to design, build, and analyze complex technology systems:
You can break down complex problems, assess system behaviors, and apply logical reasoning to find effective, scalable solutions.
You can engage in cross-disciplinary design processes, applying engineering principles to create functional systems that integrate hardware, software, data, and/or people.
You can apply theoretical knowledge in practice through hands-on work with hardware, software development, rapid prototyping, and physical troubleshooting, including participation in labs, workshops, and real-world challenges.
developed and practiced skills in scientific collaboration, communication, and writing:
You can work in diverse teams and share knowledge and perspectives to co-create solutions while demonstrating strong communication and collaboration skills.
You know how to document, present, and communicate technology concepts clearly and effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.
You can apply scientific literacy and research competence when engaging with emerging technologies.

objectives.heading: General competence
objectives.text:
After completing this programme, you will have
the ability to take responsibility for your own work and learning:
You demonstrate autonomy and self-direction by identifying opportunities, setting goals, and executing technical work independently in both academic and applied settings.
You have developed the mindset and habits of curiosity and lifelong learning and are able to build new skills to stay effective and relevant in dynamic technical environments.
competence in critical thinking and informed decision‑making:
You can apply critical thinking to analyse multifaceted challenges, define problem scopes, and articulate solution pathways that are technically and practically feasible.
You can evaluate trade-offs and make responsible decisions that balance innovation, practical impact, and ethical considerations.

overview.heading: Why choose this programme?
overview.text:
Do you see yourself shaping future energy solutions, building smart robots, or designing satellites? Still exploring your options? If you want to understand the variety of complex technology systems and learn how to build them, this programme is a great place to begin.
Photo: Erik Hansen / JS Norge.
Wondering what a technology system is, and what the people behind it do? Technology systems are coordinated networks of hardware, software, data, and people that deliver a function. They make big things happen across energy, space, robotics, healthcare, and digital infrastructure. Think robots, satellites, smart grids, or sensor networks. These systems form the basis of the smart, connected world we live in.
This international bachelor’s programme in Technology Systems: Science and Engineering is based on the “thinking in systems and thinking for systems” approach. The curriculum blends a scientific understanding of system behavior, modelling, and complexity with engineering capabilities to design, prototype, test, and iterate real-world systems. In this programme, you will gain hands‑on experience with cutting‑edge technologies. You will not just read about systems but actually create them.

objectives.heading: Help solve some of the world’s most pressing challenges
objectives.text:
This programme trains you to develop a systems mindset. Across science, engineering, and technology, you will design and deliver solutions that hold up in the real world, spanning challenges from sustainable energy to space exploration, through applied projects and interdisciplinary teamwork.
Photo: Nicolai Solbakk Willumsen.
You will have the opportunity to explore domains and learn about
renewable energy system and energy storage technologies:
why do renewable energy systems look so different in South America, Northern Norway, Africa, and Europe, and how does environment, society and law shape the energy transition?
robotics and autonomous systems:
how do we design smart machines and robots to solve real problems on land, at sea, in hospitals, and in industry?
digital security of physical systems and critical infrastructures:
how can we keep electricity systems safe from blackouts, cyberattacks, and failures in critical infrastructure?
space systems and technologies:
what does it take to send a satellite into space, from the first sketch to launch and mission control?
healthcare technologies:
how can data from the human body and machine learning transform health technology and create breakthroughs in medical innovation?

objectives.heading: Knowledge across fields and sectors = transdisciplinary systems’ approach
objectives.text:
The programme is designed to ignite your curiosity, fuel your ambition, and prepare you to make a real difference in the world. It goes beyond technical training by connecting engineering with social and environmental sciences, law, and the humanities – disciplines essential for addressing sustainability, justice, privacy, ethics, and regulation in emerging technologies.
Throughout the programme, you will combine classroom theory, lab‑based learning, interdisciplinary projects, and close collaboration with industry and research partners to develop a holistic understanding of technology in its real‑world context.
Photo: Ellen Johanne Jarli / Jarli & Jordan.

modules.heading: In-depth knowledge and great flexibility
modules.text:
The programme is designed to provide both in-depth knowledge and flexibility. You take at least 70 ECTS in theoretical and experimental courses specifically focused on systems science and engineering. Another 70 ECTS credits are dedicated to gaining knowledge and core skills in programming, mathematics, and physics. 30 ECTS credits are yours to design – you can use them to dive deeper into courses at the Department of Technology Systems (ITS), explore courses offered by other departments at the University of Oslo, or broaden your horizons through an exchange programme abroad or at another university in Norway.
A key strength of our programme is its flexibility. If you want, you may choose to specialise and deepen your competencies in one of the following technological systems: energy, space, healthcare, robotics, or cyber-physical security. However, if you have not decided yet, you will be able to explore different technology domains and discover your interests and passion on the go, through a combination of lectures, seminars, project-based work groups, and hands-on laboratory work.

careers.heading: Career opportunities and further education
careers.text:
Strong non‑academic ties ensure your studies connect directly to Norway’s industry and innovation ecosystem: As a student on this programme, you are part of the Department of Technology Systems (ITS). Here we collaborate with leading companies such as Equinor, we host one of the Norwegian Centres for Research-Based Innovation, CENSSS, and we engage with other research institutions and collaborate with public partners like Oslo University Hospital.
As a graduate of this programme, you will be well-equipped for roles such as technology systems analyst, systems designer, and technology systems advisor in both the public and the private sectors.
With a bachelor's degree in technology systems, you are qualified for several master's programmes at the University in Oslo, such as Renewable Energy Systems, Space Systems, Cybernetics and Autonomous Systems, and Security of Cyber-Physical Systems.
